description: Shared calculators referenced by modules via calculatorIds. Formula grammar: see CONTENT_FORMAT.md section 6.

calculators.name: Infusion rate from mcg/kg/min
calculators.description: Pump rate in mL/h for drugs dosed in mcg/kg/min (noradrenaline, adrenaline, dobutamine, milrinone, nitroglycerin by weight).
calculators.notes: Concentration (mcg/mL) = drug mg × 1000 ÷ syringe volume mL. 4 mg in 50 mL = 80 mcg/mL.

calculators.name: Dose from pump rate (mcg/kg/min)
calculators.description: Reverse calculation: what dose is the patient receiving at the current pump rate?

calculators.name: Infusion rate from per-kg-per-hour dose
calculators.description: Pump rate for drugs dosed per kg per hour (insulin U/kg/h, midazolam mg/kg/h, propofol mg/kg/h, fentanyl mcg/kg/h, dexmedetomidine mcg/kg/h).
calculators.notes: Use the same unit for dose and concentration (U with U/mL, mg with mg/mL, mcg with mcg/mL). Example: fixed-rate insulin 0.1 U/kg/h with 50 U in 50 mL (1 U/mL).

calculators.name: Infusion rate from a fixed hourly or per-minute dose
calculators.description: Pump rate for non-weight-based infusions such as vasopressin (U/min), labetalol (mg/min) or amiodarone (mg/h).
calculators.notes: Convert per-minute doses to per-hour first (×60). Vasopressin 0.03 U/min = 1.8 U/h; with 20 U in 50 mL (0.4 U/mL) = 4.5 mL/h.

calculators.name: Predicted (ideal) body weight
calculators.description: ARDSNet predicted body weight from height and sex. Use for tidal volume, not for most drug doses.

references.citation: ARDS Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes as compared with traditional tidal volumes for acute lung injury and ARDS. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8.
Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm 1974;8:650-5.

calculators.name: Tidal volume from predicted body weight
calculators.description: Lung-protective tidal volume (usually 6 mL/kg PBW; range 4-8).

references.citation: ARDS Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes as compared with traditional tidal volumes for acute lung injury and ARDS. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8.

calculators.notes: Interpretation band applies to the mL/kg input, not the output volume.

calculators.name: Adjusted body weight
calculators.description: IBW + 0.4 × (actual − IBW). Used for some drug doses (e.g. aminoglycosides) and nutrition in obesity.

references.citation: Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm 1974;8:650-5.

calculators.name: Body mass index
calculators.description: Weight ÷ height². Asian cut-offs differ (overweight ≥ 23, obese ≥ 25 in Indian guidance).

references.citation: Mosteller RD. Simplified calculation of body-surface area. N Engl J Med 1987;317:1098.

calculators.verify: Asian BMI cut-offs (23/25) follow Indian consensus; confirm preferred source.

calculators.name: Body surface area (Mosteller)
calculators.description: √(height cm × weight kg ÷ 3600).

references.citation: Mosteller RD. Simplified calculation of body-surface area. N Engl J Med 1987;317:1098.

calculators.name: PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio
calculators.description: Oxygenation ratio with ARDS severity bands (Berlin; PEEP ≥ 5 cmH₂O).

references.citation: ARDS Definition Task Force. Acute respiratory distress syndrome: the Berlin Definition. JAMA 2012;307:2526-33.
Matthay MA, et al. A new global definition of acute respiratory distress syndrome. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024;209:37-47.

calculators.name: SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio
calculators.description: Non-invasive oxygenation ratio; valid only when SpO₂ ≤ 97%. Global ARDS definition uses S/F ≤ 315.

references.citation: Matthay MA, et al. A new global definition of acute respiratory distress syndrome. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024;209:37-47.

calculators.name: Oxygenation index
calculators.description: OI = FiO₂(%) × mean airway pressure ÷ PaO₂.

references.citation: Ortiz RM, Cilley RE, Bartlett RH. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in pediatric respiratory failure. Pediatr Clin North Am 1987;34:39-46.

calculators.verify: OI bands are mainly paediatric/neonatal; adult thresholds are informal.

calculators.name: Driving pressure
calculators.description: Plateau pressure − PEEP (volume control, passive patient).

references.citation: Amato MBP, et al. Driving pressure and survival in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med 2015;372:747-55.

calculators.name: Static respiratory system compliance
calculators.description: Vt ÷ (Pplat − PEEP).

references.citation: Amato MBP, et al. Driving pressure and survival in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med 2015;372:747-55.

calculators.name: ROX index
calculators.description: (SpO₂/FiO₂) ÷ respiratory rate, for patients on HFNC. Assess at 2, 6 and 12 h.

interpretation.label: High risk of HFNC failure (< 3.85 at 12 h; < 2.85 at 2 h, < 3.47 at 6 h)

references.citation: Roca O, et al. An index combining respiratory rate and oxygenation to predict outcome of nasal high-flow therapy. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;199:1368-76.

calculators.name: Rapid shallow breathing index
calculators.description: RR ÷ tidal volume in litres during a spontaneous breathing trial.

references.citation: Yang KL, Tobin MJ. A prospective study of indexes predicting the outcome of trials of weaning from mechanical ventilation. N Engl J Med 1991;324:1445-50.

calculators.name: Alveolar-arterial O₂ gradient
calculators.description: PAO₂ = FiO₂ × (Patm − 47) − PaCO₂/0.8; A-a = PAO₂ − PaO₂.

references.citation: Albert MS, Dell RB, Winters RW. Quantitative displacement of acid-base equilibrium in metabolic acidosis. Ann Intern Med 1967;66:312-22.

calculators.notes: Expected upper limit on room air ≈ age/4 + 4 mmHg. Less reliable at high FiO₂.
calculators.verify: Reference attached is generic; add a physiology textbook citation.

calculators.name: Oxygen cylinder duration
calculators.description: Minutes of oxygen left at a given flow.

interpretation.label: Under 30 min: arrange a replacement now
Adequate for short transfer; keep 30 min reserve

calculators.notes: Default 1500 L ≈ Indian B-type medical O₂ cylinder (≈ 1.5 m³). Capacities vary by type and filler; read the cylinder label, or use o2-cylinder-contents (water capacity × pressure). Keep a 30-minute reserve.
calculators.verify: Confirm typical Indian cylinder capacities (B-type ≈ 1.5 m³, D-type ≈ 7 m³ for large cylinders) used in your hospital.

calculators.name: Oxygen cylinder contents (Boyle's law)
calculators.description: Free gas volume ≈ water capacity (L) × gauge pressure (bar). 1 kg/cm² ≈ 0.98 bar; 1 bar ≈ 14.5 psi.

interpretation.label: Use o2-cylinder-duration with your flow rate

calculators.notes: Ignores gas compressibility (slight overestimate at high pressure). Gauges in kg/cm² read almost the same as bar; psi ÷ 14.5 = bar.
calculators.verify: Check the water capacity stamped on your cylinders (B-type commonly ≈ 10 L).

calculators.name: Maintenance fluid rate (4-2-1 rule)
calculators.description: Holliday-Segar hourly maintenance: 4 mL/kg/h for the first 10 kg, 2 mL/kg/h for the next 10 kg, 1 mL/kg/h for each kg above 20.

references.citation: Holliday MA, Segar WE. The maintenance need for water in parenteral fluid therapy. Pediatrics 1957;19:823-32.

calculators.notes: Use isotonic fluid with glucose in children. In sick adults this overestimates needs (25-30 mL/kg/day is usual; 70 kg ≈ 75-90 mL/h) and enteral feeds and drug diluents count. Fluid-restrict in SIADH, cardiac/renal failure, raised ICP.

calculators.name: Paediatric endotracheal tube size
calculators.description: Internal diameter (mm) = age/4 + 3.5 (cuffed) or age/4 + 4 (uncuffed), for children ≥ 2 years.

references.citation: Van de Voorde P, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Paediatric Life Support. Resuscitation 2021;161:327-87.

calculators.notes: Round to the nearest 0.5 mm and keep one size above and below ready. Under 2 years: term neonate 3.0-3.5 uncuffed / 3.0 cuffed; infant 3.0-3.5 cuffed. Depth: see paeds-ett-depth.

calculators.name: Paediatric oral ETT depth at the lips
calculators.description: Oral tube depth (cm at lips) = age/2 + 12 for children ≥ 2 years (≈ 3 × ETT ID).

references.citation: Van de Voorde P, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Paediatric Life Support. Resuscitation 2021;161:327-87.

calculators.notes: Nasal tube: age/2 + 15. Always confirm with capnography, auscultation and chest X-ray (tip at T2-T3).
calculators.verify: Formula is the widely taught APLS rule; confirm against your local PALS/APLS chart.

calculators.name: Paediatric weight estimate (APLS)
calculators.description: 1-5 years: 2 × age + 8. 6-12 years: 3 × age + 7.

references.citation: Luscombe M, Owens B. Weight estimation in resuscitation: is the current formula still valid? Arch Dis Child 2007;92:412-5.

calculators.notes: Infants < 12 months: (0.5 × age in months) + 4. Tick 'Age 6-12 years' for older children (formula becomes 3 × age + 7). Use measured weight or a length-based tape (Broselow) when available; Indian children are often lighter than these UK-derived estimates.
calculators.verify: APLS formulas may overestimate weight in undernourished Indian children; prefer measured weight.

calculators.name: Westley croup score
calculators.description: Severity of croup (0-17).

interpretation.label: ≥ 12: impending respiratory failure – senior airway help

references.citation: Westley CR, Cotton EK, Brooks JG. Nebulized racemic epinephrine by IPPB for the treatment of croup: a double-blind study. Am J Dis Child 1978;132:484-7.

calculators.name: Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS v2.0)
calculators.description: Baseline frailty 2 weeks before acute illness, scored 1-9. Validated for age ≥ 65.

interpretation.label: 7-9: severe frailty or terminally ill: discuss goals of care

references.citation: Rockwood K, et al. A global clinical measure of fitness and frailty in elderly people. CMAJ 2005;173:489-95.
Rockwood K, Theou O. Using the Clinical Frailty Scale in allocating scarce health care resources. Can Geriatr J 2020;23:210-5.

calculators.notes: Score the baseline, not the acute state. Not validated for younger people or stable single-limb disability. Use as one input to shared decisions, never as a sole triage rule.

calculators.name: STOP-BANG
calculators.description: Screening for obstructive sleep apnoea (0-8).
calculators.formula: snore + tired + observed + pressure + bmi + age + neck + male

interpretation.label: 5-8: high risk: plan for difficult mask ventilation, opioid-sparing, post-extubation CPAP/NIV

references.citation: Chung F, et al. STOP questionnaire: a tool to screen patients for obstructive sleep apnea. Anesthesiology 2008;108:812-21.

calculators.notes: Asian populations: some studies use BMI > 30 or neck > 38 cm cut-offs; the original thresholds are kept here.

calculators.name: Anion gap
calculators.description: Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻). Correct for albumin.

interpretation.label: Low: check albumin, lab error, myeloma, lithium/bromide

references.citation: Figge J, Jabor A, Kazda A, Fencl V. Anion gap and hypoalbuminemia. Crit Care Med 1998;26:1807-10.

calculators.verify: Normal AG range depends on the analyser; use the local lab range.

calculators.name: Albumin-corrected anion gap
calculators.description: AG + 2.5 × (4.0 − albumin g/dL).

references.citation: Figge J, Jabor A, Kazda A, Fencl V. Anion gap and hypoalbuminemia. Crit Care Med 1998;26:1807-10.

calculators.name: Delta ratio
calculators.description: (AG − 12) ÷ (24 − HCO₃⁻). Detects a second metabolic process in a high-AG acidosis.

interpretation.label: Pure high-AG acidosis (1-2; DKA can be ≈ 1)
High-AG acidosis plus metabolic alkalosis or chronic respiratory acidosis

references.citation: Figge J, Jabor A, Kazda A, Fencl V. Anion gap and hypoalbuminemia. Crit Care Med 1998;26:1807-10.

calculators.verify: Reference is for AG/albumin; add a delta-ratio source (e.g. LITFL/Rastegar).

calculators.name: Expected PaCO₂ (Winter's formula)
calculators.description: Expected PaCO₂ = 1.5 × HCO₃⁻ + 8 (± 2) in metabolic acidosis.

references.citation: Albert MS, Dell RB, Winters RW. Quantitative displacement of acid-base equilibrium in metabolic acidosis. Ann Intern Med 1967;66:312-22.

calculators.notes: Measured PaCO₂ above the range = additional respiratory acidosis; below = additional respiratory alkalosis.

calculators.name: Calculated serum osmolality (Indian units)
calculators.description: 2 × Na + glucose (mg/dL)/18 + urea (mg/dL)/6. Uses blood urea, as reported by most Indian labs.

references.citation: Hillier TA, Abbott RD, Barrett EJ. Hyponatremia: evaluating the correction factor for hyperglycemia. Am J Med 1999;106:399-403.

calculators.notes: If your lab reports BUN instead of urea: urea = BUN × 2.14, or use BUN/2.8.

calculators.name: Osmolal gap
calculators.description: Measured − calculated osmolality. Raised in toxic alcohol poisoning.

interpretation.label: Raised: consider methanol, ethylene glycol, ethanol, mannitol

references.citation: Hillier TA, Abbott RD, Barrett EJ. Hyponatremia: evaluating the correction factor for hyperglycemia. Am J Med 1999;106:399-403.

calculators.verify: A normal osmolal gap does not exclude late toxic alcohol poisoning.

calculators.name: Sodium corrected for glucose
calculators.description: Na + 2.4 × (glucose − 100)/100 (Hillier; Katz uses 1.6).

references.citation: Hillier TA, Abbott RD, Barrett EJ. Hyponatremia: evaluating the correction factor for hyperglycemia. Am J Med 1999;106:399-403.

calculators.name: Expected Na change per litre of infusate (Adrogue-Madias)
calculators.description: ΔNa = (infusate Na + K − serum Na) ÷ (TBW + 1). Estimate only; recheck Na every 2-4 h.

references.citation: Adrogue HJ, Madias NE. Hyponatremia. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1581-9.
Spasovski G, et al. Clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia. Eur J Endocrinol 2014;170:G1-47.

calculators.notes: 3% saline = 513 mmol/L Na; 0.9% saline = 154; Ringer's lactate ≈ 130 (+4 K); D5W = 0. Limit correction to ≤ 10 mmol/L in 24 h (≤ 8 if high risk of osmotic demyelination).

calculators.name: Free water deficit

references.citation: Adrogue HJ, Madias NE. Hyponatremia. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1581-9.

calculators.notes: Add ongoing losses. In chronic hypernatraemia lower Na by ≤ 10-12 mmol/L per 24 h.

calculators.name: Albumin-corrected calcium
calculators.description: Ca (mg/dL) + 0.8 × (4.0 − albumin g/dL). Prefer ionised calcium in ICU.

references.citation: Payne RB, et al. Interpretation of serum calcium in patients with abnormal serum proteins. Br Med J 1973;4:643-6.

calculators.name: Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault)
calculators.description: (140 − age) × weight ÷ (72 × creatinine), × 0.85 if female. Not valid in unstable AKI.

references.citation: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron 1976;16:31-41.

calculators.notes: Use actual weight if below IBW; consider adjusted weight in obesity.

calculators.name: Fractional excretion of sodium
calculators.description: (Urine Na × Plasma Cr) ÷ (Plasma Na × Urine Cr) × 100.

references.citation: Espinel CH. The FENa test: use in the differential diagnosis of acute renal failure. JAMA 1976;236:579-81.

calculators.name: Mean arterial pressure
calculators.description: (SBP + 2 × DBP) ÷ 3 (estimate; use the arterial line value when available).

references.citation: Singer M, et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315:801-10.

calculators.name: Shock index
calculators.description: Heart rate ÷ systolic BP.

references.citation: Allgower M, Burri C. Shock index. Dtsch Med Wochenschr 1967;92:1947-50.

calculators.name: Corrected QT (Bazett)
calculators.description: QT ÷ √(RR in seconds). Over-corrects at fast heart rates.

references.citation: Bazett HC. An analysis of the time-relations of electrocardiograms. Heart 1920;7:353-70.

calculators.name: Burns fluid in first 24 h
calculators.description: mL/kg/%TBSA × weight × %TBSA (partial + full thickness). Half in the first 8 h from the time of burn.

references.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Student Course Manual, 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018.

calculators.notes: ATLS 10th ed. starts adults at 2 mL/kg/%TBSA (Parkland formula uses 4). Titrate to urine output 0.5 mL/kg/h (1 mL/kg/h in electrical injury).

calculators.name: Glasgow Coma Scale
calculators.description: Eye + Verbal + Motor (3-15). Record components, e.g. E3 V4 M5.

references.citation: Teasdale G, et al. The Glasgow Coma Scale at 40 years: standing the test of time. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:844-54.

calculators.notes: If a component is untestable (e.g. intubated), record NT/T and do not sum.

calculators.name: qSOFA
calculators.description: Bedside prompt for poor outcome in suspected infection. Not a diagnostic test for sepsis.

interpretation.label: ≥ 2: higher risk of poor outcome; assess for organ dysfunction

references.citation: Singer M, et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315:801-10.
Prescott HC, Antonelli M, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Med. 2026;52(5):863-936.

calculators.notes: SSC 2026 recommends NEWS, NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS over qSOFA as a single screening tool (strong, moderate certainty). A positive qSOFA still signals higher risk.

calculators.name: SOFA score
calculators.description: Sequential Organ Failure Assessment: 0-4 per organ system, total 0-24. A rise of ≥ 2 from baseline with infection = sepsis.
calculators.formula: resp + coag + liver + cvs + cns + renal

references.citation: Vincent JL, et al. The SOFA (Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment) score to describe organ dysfunction/failure. Intensive Care Med 1996;22:707-10.
Singer M, et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315:801-10.

calculators.verify: An updated SOFA-2 score was published in 2025; decide whether the app should use original SOFA, SOFA-2 or both. Severity bands here are descriptive, not validated mortality cut-offs.

calculators.name: NEWS2
calculators.description: National Early Warning Score 2 (SpO₂ scale 1).

options.label: New confusion, voice, pain or unresponsive

calculators.formula: rr + spo2 + o2 + sbp + hr + avpu + temp

interpretation.label: 0-4: low (a single parameter scoring 3 = low-medium: urgent ward review)
≥ 7: high: emergency response / critical care team

references.citation: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2. London: RCP; 2017.

calculators.name: CURB-65
calculators.description: Severity of community-acquired pneumonia.

inputs.label: Urea > 7 mmol/L (blood urea > 42 mg/dL; BUN > 19 mg/dL)

references.citation: Lim WS, et al. Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study. Thorax 2003;58:377-82.

calculators.name: Wells score for PE
calculators.description: Pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism.

inputs.label: Immobilisation ≥ 3 days or surgery in past 4 weeks

calculators.formula: dvt + likely + hr + immob + prior + haemoptysis + cancer

references.citation: Wells PS, et al. Derivation of a simple clinical model to categorize patients probability of pulmonary embolism. Thromb Haemost 2000;83:416-20.

calculators.notes: Boolean inputs contribute their 'points' value when true.

calculators.name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale
calculators.description: Single-item sedation/agitation score from +4 to −5.

options.label: −3 Moderate sedation (movement to voice, no eye contact)
−4 Deep sedation (movement to physical stimulation only)

interpretation.label: Light to moderate sedation (target usually −2 to 0)
Agitated: look for pain, delirium, hypoxia, withdrawal

references.citation: Sessler CN, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;166:1338-44.

calculators.name: Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning (POP) scale
calculators.description: Severity of OP poisoning at presentation (0-11).

options.label: Impaired, no response to verbal commands

calculators.formula: pupil + fasc + resp + hr + loc + seizure

references.citation: Senanayake N, et al. A proposed oral poisoning scale: Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning (POP) scale. In: Senanayake N, ed. Clinical toxicology. 1993.

calculators.verify: Confirm the six POP items and the seizure item (some versions list 5 items scoring 0-10).
